purpose: Amendment to the frozen T9d FP32/MPS protocol v2 (via the v3 two-arm amendment and the v4 LoRA amendment): retrain the winning W45 arm — LoRA r16 on a frozen backbone — on engineering-judgment corpus v4 (4320 items / 2376 train / 36 families / 720 source groups, including high-cardinality 32- and 255-candidate choice families). The corpus-v4 manifest status is 'training_data_prerequisite_no_training_authorized'; this amendment is the required new authorization-binding protocol. Everything else (warm start, optimizer, objective, loss, selection rule, reporting rule) is inherited verbatim.

Readout is not the binding constraint; corpus scale/diversity is the higher-value axis (motivates X4 corpus v4 and this retrain).

design.freeze_backbone: via --lora-rank (base weights never require grad; --backbone-lr 0 required and accepted)
design.steps_justification: Corpus v4 train is 2376 rows vs v3's 1080 (2.2x). At --batch-questions 16, 300 steps = 4800 question-draws = only ~2.0 epochs at v4 scale vs ~4.4 epochs in the proven v3 run — keeping 300 would confound 'more data' with 'half the training exposure'. The three v3 dev minima occurred at steps 150/200/250 = 2.2/3.0/3.7 epochs of v3 exposure. 600 steps = 9600 draws = ~4.0 epochs at v4 scale, bracketing the epoch range where all v3 minima occurred plus margin, while dev-minimum selection makes excess budget self-correcting and the inherited last-point rule honestly reports budget exhaustion if the minimum lands on the final evaluation point.
design.eval_every_justification: Unchanged from protocol v2/W45: at v4 scale a dev evaluation (756 questions, packed forward passes on MPS) costs ~10-20s against ~45-60s of training per 50-step block, so a finer cadence is cheap; keeping the identical cadence preserves comparability with the v3 LoRA arm's evaluation lattice and gives 12 registered evaluation points for min localization.
design.max_microbatch_tokens_justification: REQUIRED change vs protocol v2's 16384: corpus v4's batch_grid_255 family emits 255-candidate choice questions whose complete-question footprint is 255 padded paths x ~110 tokens = up to 29070 tokens, exceeding 16384. The trainer's contract forbids splitting a question's softmax across microbatches (pack_complete_questions raises rather than splits), and its pre-flight pack check over all splits fails closed. 32768 is the smallest power-of-two budget covering the measured maximum (29070) with ~13% headroom; it changes only the memory envelope and packing granularity, never the loss, normalization or update rule. 255-path questions always pack alone (2 x 29070 > 32768); all other questions pack as before under microbatch_questions=4.

data_contract.validated_by: train_pipeline_decisions_v4.py --validate-only: 4320 records, all 4320 questions eligible for gold_distribution (run 2026-09-20)
data_contract.no_external_model_outputs: Corpus v4 contains NO external model outputs: every gold/gold_probs is computed by the family's frozen programmatic oracle (deterministic_truth one-hot or programmatic_conditional_distribution); the manifest records provenance.derived_from_any_existing_evaluation_record=false, uses_evaluation_corpus_as_source=false, refused_path_marker_count=23 and reserved_token_count=30 enforced at build; Jev outputs from any source never enter training data per AGENTS.md publication discipline. There is no teacher arm in this run and no teacher field is consumed.

heldout_v1.role: independent heldout; evaluation only, never trained on; comparability anchor to all prior arms

heldout_v2.predict_input_derivation: deterministic view derived once from items.jsonl: states = [{id, state, questions}] per row; written before any checkpoint read of this heldout
heldout_v2.role: independent heldout; evaluation only, never trained on; larger (312q / 104 groups / 13 families) honest check vs the 69q v1 noise band

data_contract.heldout_read_once_rule: Each heldout file is read for inference exactly ONCE per selected checkpoint (per seed), plus once for the atomic warm-start checkpoint as the heldout_v2 reference baseline. No heldout file is read during training, for selection, or iteratively for tuning; a failed/interrupted predict call may be retried but no metric-driven re-evaluation is permitted.

selection_and_reporting.selection_metric: target cross-entropy (inherited from protocol v2, unchanged)
selection_and_reporting.last_point_rule: If the minimum is the final registered evaluation point, report budget exhaustion and lack of convergence; do not add steps after observing results.
post_run_evaluation: heldout_v1 predict per seed via scripts/predict_toy_decisions.py (fp32/mps, batch-questions 8, max-length 2048) -> results/heldout_v1_post_v5_lora_seed{N}.json; accuracy, coverage@0.9, per-type breakdown, mean confidence vs the 0.464 G4 baseline (results/heldout_v1_g4_baseline.json) and the v3 LoRA arm (mean 0.536, best 0.580)

heldout_v2 predict per seed via the same harness -> results/heldout_v2_post_v5_lora_seed{N}.json; same metrics; reference = atomic warm-start checkpoint scored once on heldout_v2 -> results/heldout_v2_atomic_seed17.json
corpus v4 test accuracy per question type from predictions_test.jsonl in each run dir

selection_and_reporting.mps_contention_rule: No predict or lifecycle calls while a training run occupies MPS; evaluations run strictly after each arm completes. Lifecycle timeouts during training are a known phenomenon, not a failure.

honest_prior.statement: W45 showed LoRA r16 is the best arm at v3 scale (heldout 0.536 mean) but within the n=69 noise band of head-only. Corpus v4 is 2.2x larger with 2x the families and the first wide-cardinality coverage (32/255 candidates); heldout_v2 (312q) halves the noise band vs v1. Prior belief: a modest improvement over the v3 arm is plausible but not assured — v4 adds harder family types (negation, lotteries, wide grids) that may lower absolute scores even while generalization improves; a flat or negative result is an honest outcome and does not invalidate the corpus.

preregistered_interpretation.v5_beats_v3_on_both_heldouts: corpus scale/diversity was the binding constraint (X2 prediction confirmed); next lever is J-C selective-risk machinery on this checkpoint and/or rank/step sweep
preregistered_interpretation.v5_flat_vs_v3: corpus scale alone does not move heldout at this capacity; next levers are LoRA rank, steps, or representation-level approaches
preregistered_interpretation.v5_below_v3: v4's harder families hurt transfer or the wider token budget changed effective training; inspect per-type/per-family dev and test metrics before any conclusion; do not retrain on observation
